solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Painfully twist alien insect

parts.note: to crick your neck is to twist or rick it painfully
ET is the film's extraterrestrial, a stock alien

explanation.surface: Someone wrenches an extraterrestrial bug with cruel force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painfully twist' reads as an instruction to the solver, but it is a verb meaning crick.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirping, jumping creature related to the grasshopper is an example of an insect.

clue.text: Manure's price limiting order pressure

indicators.note: limiting means the price word hems in the other letters

parts.note: cost means price
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Manure's price restricts the pressure that orders can exert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limiting' is a containment signal; the Order of Merit is a British honour, hence 'order' gives its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotted organic matter used to enrich soil is a fertiliser like manure.

clue.text: Popular jazz musician who helps criminals

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a sideman is a supporting player in a jazz band

explanation.surface: A well-liked jazz player turns out to aid criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: A sideman is a band member who is not the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone placed inside an organisation to help crooks commit a robbery or fraud is their accomplice on the staff.

clue.text: Fighting with sticks to finish in knockout

indicators.note: in means the finishing word is placed inside the knockout

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for a knockout
end means to finish

explanation.surface: A stick fight ends with someone knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the containment signal; 'to finish' is a verb phrase, not an instruction to take a last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese martial art is fencing with bamboo swords, so it is fighting with sticks.

clue.text: Comes across poetry after erecting sculptures?

indicators.note: after means the poetry follows the other piece
erecting, in a down clue, sets the word upright so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: sculptures are examples of art, hence the question mark
verses are lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on poetry after putting up statues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erecting' works as a reversal only because this is a down clue, read upwards; 'after' orders the pieces. The question mark flags sculptures as an example of art.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross a stretch of ground is to traverse it, so 'comes across' in the sense of crossing fits.

clue.text: Orc remains in an oddly large group of islands

indicators.note: oddly tells us to keep the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and so on, of the words before it

explanation.surface: A fantasy monster stays put on a far-flung archipelago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like an adverb about the group of islands, but it signals taking alternate letters from 'Orc remains in an'.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers the Pacific region of islands including Melanesia, Micronesia and Polynesia, so it is a vast island group.

clue.text: Nothing against a liberal society giving Australian grounds for 1 across

parts.note: O is the zero digit, nothing
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: A permissive, zero-tolerance society gives Australians a reason for playing cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounds' looks like reasons, but it means sports fields; 1 across is CRICKET.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia cricket and football fields are often oval in shape and are commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Corrected errors European people saw

parts.note: men means people
dated means saw someone romantically, went out with

explanation.surface: A European saw people's mistakes being fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' is not the past of see in its usual sense, but 'was seeing', i.e. went out with.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to remove its mistakes, so this rarer form means fixed errors.

clue.text: Veil primarily needed in Qatar and Bahrain

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A face covering is mainly required in two Gulf states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes the opening letters of 'needed in Qatar and Bahrain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A face covering with a slit for the eyes, worn by some Muslim women, is a kind of veil.

clue.text: Squares accounts with senior churchman in time

indicators.note: in means the churchman's title is placed inside the word for time

parts.note: ages means a long time
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A senior cleric settles scores with someone in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the containment signal; Ven (Venerable) is the formal title of an archdeacon in the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To take revenge is to pay someone back, which the idiom 'squares accounts with' expresses.

clue.text: Mother with child who is on the square

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A mum and her little one stand in the town square.
explanation.walkthrough: Freemasons describe a fellow member as being 'on the square', from the square that is one of their symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'on the square' is Freemasons' slang for belonging to the brotherhood, so the phrase describes a Freemason.

clue.text: Lincoln opens strange square artwork

indicators.note: Lincoln opens the jumble by going into the middle of it
strange means the letters of the following word are put into an odd new order

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of US President Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: Abraham Lincoln unveils a peculiar piece of art in a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' scrambles the square and 'opens' signals the president going inside the jumble; 'square' looks like the place but is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornate design of interlacing scrolls and foliage is a kind of decorative artwork.

clue.text: Squares of gold? Yes, could be

indicators.note: could be invites us to rearrange the words before it into a possible other form

explanation.surface: Asks whether people who are squares might be made of gold, and answers yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges the letters of 'of gold yes'; 'Squares' here are dull, conventional people, not shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Squares in slang are conventional, unfashionable people, the same as stuffy old-fashioned types.

clue.text: Remove trousers with wrong badge

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of the following word are set out incorrectly, in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to drop their trousers for wearing the wrong badge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges BADGE. The answer is old British schoolboy slang for pulling someone's trousers off as a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang, chiefly from schools and universities, for pulling down or stripping off someone's trousers as a prank.

clue.text: By square familiar to 17 …

definitions.meaning: in arithmetic, 'by' means multiplied by, as in three by four
17 is NEW YORKER, and the famous Manhattan square they know is the one at Broadway and Seventh Avenue

explanation.surface: Points out a square that the clue-17 people know well.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 15, which reverses this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means multiplied by, and it is also the name of the famous square in Manhattan.

clue.text: Calm note about German national park

indicators.note: about means the calm and note words go around the German

parts.note: serene means calm
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A peaceful German notes something about a national park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts G inside SERENETI, after SEREN.
explanation.definitionFit: This Tanzanian plain famous for its wildlife migration is a protected national park.

clue.text: … back with nose broken at regular intervals

indicators.note: back means the previous answer is written in reverse order

parts.note: the ellipsis stands for the answer to 13, the multiplying word

indicators.note: broken means the letters of nose are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's nose is broken repeatedly, at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: The '…' carries over 13's answer, TIMES; 'back' reverses it to SEMIT, and 'broken' turns NOSE into ONES.
explanation.definitionFit: These half-steps are the equal, regular musical intervals that divide the octave into twelve in Western tuning.

clue.text: Detailed article in Gramophone cut short and mangled

indicators.note: mangled means the remaining letters are wrecked into a new order
cut short means the last letter of the word is lopped off

explanation.surface: A long magazine piece about gramophones is abridged and garbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the final E from GRAMOPHONE, and 'mangled' rearranges GRAMOPHON.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarly treatise on a single specialised subject is a detailed written study.

clue.text: Knee worry sorted out by magazine

indicators.note: sorted out means the letters before it are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A magazine sorts out a reader's worry about their knee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges 'Knee worry'.
explanation.definitionFit: This weekly American periodical famous for cartoons and long journalism is a well-known magazine.

clue.text: Revolves around rents once revised

indicators.note: revised means the letters of the preceding words are reworked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A conversation that keeps returning to rents that were once changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges the letters of 'rents once'.
explanation.definitionFit: If a discussion focuses on one topic it revolves around it, so the phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: See promo silent about independent element

parts.note: see is said like the letter C, a common crossword stand-in for it
an ad, like a promo, is a promotion or advertisement

indicators.note: about means the silent word wraps around the independent letter

parts.note: mum means silent, as in 'keep mum'

explanation.surface: Look at an advertisement that stays quiet about a free-standing element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside MUM to make MIUM. 'See' gives C, the letter whose name it sounds like.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft bluish metal, atomic number 48, is a chemical element.

clue.text: Penny has swallows

parts.note: D was the abbreviation for the pre-decimal British penny, from Latin denarius
owns means has or possesses

explanation.surface: A woman called Penny keeps some birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' looks like the birds, but it is the verb, as in gulping a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To down a drink is to gulp or swallow it, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Cooked for horse to eat in the morning

indicators.note: to eat means the horse takes the morning inside itself

parts.note: a steed is a horse
AM, ante meridiem, means the morning

explanation.surface: Something was cooked for a horse to eat at breakfast time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' is a containment signal: the horse swallows the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Food cooked over boiling water has been prepared by this method, so it is a kind of cooking.

clue.text: Medical man with beard all square

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, a medical man
an awn is the bristly beard on an ear of barley or other grass

explanation.surface: A bearded doctor ends a game level with his opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beard' is not facial hair but the bristles on a cereal grain.
explanation.definitionFit: A game that ends all square is tied, with neither side winning.

clue.text: American not believable in any way

parts.note: tall, as in a tall story, means hard to believe

explanation.surface: An American is not believable in any respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not believable' is TALL, as in a tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an intensifier in negatives, as in 'not in the least', meaning in any way whatever.

clue.text: In square, I get honey ordered

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of the preceding words are arranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone collects honey in a town square, put in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges 'I get honey'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine times nine gives this number, so it is an example of a perfect square.

clue.text: Water from stone via nuclearisation

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Water drawn from stone through a nuclear process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes letters running across 'stonE VIA Nuclearisation'.
explanation.definitionFit: This French mineral water from the shores of Lake Geneva is a well-known bottled brand.

clue.text: Square instrument making a sharp point

parts.note: a T-square is a draughtsman's square, so the letter T stands for it
a horn is a brass musical instrument

explanation.surface: A square musical instrument has a sharp end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' gives T, from the T-square shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A spike on a rose stem is a sharp, pointed growth on a plant.

clue.text: CIA remain problematic where they are based

indicators.note: problematic suggests something awry, so the preceding letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: The CIA staying put is a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problematic' rearranges 'CIA remain'; 'they' are the CIA from the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Central Intelligence Agency has its headquarters in the United States, so this phrase says where it is based.

clue.text: Chinese leader goes round country backing tarred rope

indicators.note: backing means the whole assembled string is reversed
goes round means the leader's name wraps itself around the country

parts.note: Mao Zedong was the leader of Communist China
UK is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: Mao tours a country and supports a rope industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes round' sets the country inside the leader's name, giving MUKAO, and 'backing' then reverses the whole string.
explanation.definitionFit: This loose hemp fibre picked from old tarred ropes was used to caulk ship seams, so it is tarred rope.

clue.text: Square mark on the Italian hero

parts.note: M is short for the old German currency the mark
il is the Italian word for 'the'
a lion is a brave person or celebrated hero, as in 'literary lion'

explanation.surface: A town square bears a mark honouring an Italian hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just puts M before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: This number is a thousand times a thousand, so it is a perfect square.

clue.text: Area of local government once square

definitions.meaning: historically an English county was divided into these subdivisions, each with its own court
the number ten times ten, a perfect square

explanation.surface: Recalls an old local-government district that was once a square.
explanation.walkthrough: English counties were once divided into subdivisions with this name, still remembered in the parliamentary Chiltern Hundreds.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an old county subdivision and also the number that is ten squared.
